Judgment:
The appellant is claimant in M.V.O.P.No.887of 2002 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge at Vizianagaram, and the respondents are the respondents in the said case.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge at Vizianagaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimant has filed a claim petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- for the injuries sustained and disability suffered by him in a motor vehicle accident, that occurred on 10.02.2002 at about 11:00 A.M.
4.

The case of the petitioner is as follows:
On 10.02.2002 at about 11:00 a.m., after purchasing rice at Vizianagaram, while he is returning to his village on his Bajaj Moped bearing No. AP 35 B 5473, while he reached near Balaji junction, the 1st respondent drove the van from RTC Complex,
Vizianagaram in a rash and negligent manner with high speed without blowing horn and dashed the Moped, the petitioner further pleaded that as a result, he fell down on the road and received fracture injuries on his right leg and multiple injuries all over his body and immediately he was taken to the private clinic of Dr.A.Sreeramamurthy,
Orthopedic Surgeon, where he underwent operation for his fracture injury.
He further pleaded, after discharging, he also joined in the Government Head Quarters Hospital, Vizianagaram on 20.03.2002.

and he is doing kirana business used to earn Rs.200/- per day, and because of the accident he suffered severe mental agony and he spent more Money towards medical expenses.
5. The 1st and 2nd respondents are remained ex parte.
6. The 3rd respondent filed counter denying the allegations in the petition.
He further pleaded that the petitioner was not having a valid driving license.

The vehicle was not having a valid Insurance coverage at the time of accident, due to the contributory negligence of the petitioner, the accident took place and hence the third respondent has no liability to pay the compensation.

sentences.text:
7. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1) Whether the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the 4194?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation?
3) Whether the respondents are liable to pay any compensation?
4) To what relief?
8.
On behalf of the petitioner, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A9 and Ex.X1 were marked.
on behalf of third respondent, RW1 and RW2 were examined and Ex.B1 and B4 were marked.
Basing on the material on record, the learned Tribunal dismissed the claim application on 08.08.2006 vide its order dated 08.08.2006, against which the present appeal is filed by claimant.

9. Now the point for consideration is:
Whether the Order of the Tribunal needs any interference?

POINT:
10.

In order to prove the claim of the petitioner, the petitioner himself examined as PW1, as per his evidence 10.02.2002 at about 11:00 a.m., while he was returning on a Bajaj Moped from Vizianagaram Market to his village and when his vehicle reached Balaji Junction, one Van being driven by the driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from RTC Complex side dashed his moped, he sustained fractures of bones of right foot besides other injuries all over his body.
As per his evidence immediately after the accident he was taken to the private hospital of Dr.Sreerama Murthy, he was treated as an in-patient for twenty two days, an operation was performed.
One week after discharge he joined in M.R. Government Hospital as the injury did not heal.

11. As per the case of the petitioner immediately after the accident, he was treated as an in-patient for a period of 22 days in Dr. Sreeramamurthy Hospital, an operation was performed, but he failed to examined said Dr.Sreeramamurthy as a witness before the Tribunal and in order to prove the injuries immediate to the accident, he failed to examine the said Dr.Sreeramamurthy as a witness.

12. The 3rd respondent severally pleaded that, the petitioner failed to prove because of the road accident he sustained injuries, the respondent also marked certified copy of wound certificate of the petitioner as Ex.B3, the petitioner also marked attested copy of wound certificate as Ex.A3, in Ex.A3,
the date of accident was altered from 09.02.2002 to 10.02.2002.
In Ex.B3 wound certificate, the date of accident was mentioned as on 09.02.2002.

As per the case of the petitioner the accident was occurred on 10.02.2002, there is discrepancy with regard to the date of accident the said Bandaru Venkati Yellaji vs Dondasana Santoshkumar Amp 2 Ors on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36358572/
2 discrepancy is not at all explained by the claim petitioner.

sentences.text:
13. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner examined the one Government Doctor,
who treated in the Government Hospital as PW2, as per his evidence, the injuries were caused on 10.02.2002 and that there was a correction of the figure '9' to '10' and the petitioner was examined him on 20.03.2002 at 03:45 p.m. i.e. about forty days after the accident.
He further admits in the wound certificate it was mentioned, that the injury was two weeks old.

As per the evidence of PW2,
he examined the claim petitioner on 20.03.2002 i.e., after a lapse of 40 days from the date alleged accident.

The petitioner failed to examined the said Dr. Sreeramamurthy as a witness, and the petitioner also did not file any case sheet maintained in the private Hospital, the petitioner did not file any medical record to show that he underwent treatment in a private nursing home at Vizianagaram.
The petitioner failed to give any explanation with regard to the discrepancies as regards the date of accident.
As per the evidence of PW2 doctor, he treated the petitioner after forty days of the accident.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove the Ex.A2 injuries.
As per Ex.A2, the doctor treated the petitioner after 40 days of the accident.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that because of the accident occurred on 10.02.2002, he received injuries.
But he failed to adduce any evidence.
14. The petitioner approached the Tribunal for claim of Rs.1,50,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident.
The initial burden on the petitioner to prove the accident and so also because of the accident, he sustained injuries in a road accident.
This Court has clearly stated above there is a discrepancy with regard to the date of accident.
As per the evidence of PW2 Government Doctor, the petitioner was treated in a government hospital on 20.03.2002 i.e., after lapse of 40 days from the date of accident.
He admits that in the wound certificate it was mentioned that the injury was two weeks old.

15. Therefore, the petitioner failed to prove that, because of the road accident, he sustained injuries and he entitled claim from the respondents the Tribunal by giving cogent reasons and dismissed the claim application.

Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the finding given by the Tribunal,
therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation.
The learned Tribunal by passing cogent reasons dismissed the claim application.
There is no need to interfere with the finding given by the Tribunal in its Order.
16. In the result, this appeal is dismissed by confirming the order dated 08.08.2006 in M.V.O.P.No.887of 2002 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge at Vizianagaram.
